annotationRationale: The main route directly constructs four representatives per center color. The alternative counts distinguished-position grids and explains why symmetric and nonsymmetric grids have different class sizes. Both routes justify all local restrictions and all symmetry identifications without requiring an abstract graph model or an advanced counting theorem.

review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful accessible routes are present: construct canonical representatives, or count oriented grids and distinguish symmetry sizes. No additional method is needed.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed coloring and symmetry nodes are precise. Combined counting is appropriate support. Removing the former graph-models support is justified because neither method constructs an abstract graph.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The forced chain correctly leaves only the bottom row. Bottom-middle blue is impossible; yellow gives bottom rows BYR and BYB; red gives BRR and BRY. Each completed grid is valid. The unique blue side square restricts possible identifications to horizontal reflection, which either breaks normalization or fixes BRY. Thus there are four classes per center color and 12 altogether.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The supplied Random Math reference supports this route. The candidate uses original explanatory prose, strengthens the normalization proof, and correctly requires the forced blue corner to neighbor yellow, despite the reference's stray statement about red. The source-informed-original designation is honest; no official MAA authorship is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why local forcing helps. Every forced color, remaining case, and possible symmetry identification is explained sufficiently for an AMC 10 learner.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three immediate nodes are used: adjacency-constrained coloring, justified representatives under symmetry, and addition followed by multiplication in the class count.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The forced chain proves that a blue side has yellow opposite and a red side adjacent, excluding every other blue side. With blue on the right, the side patterns give 3, 2, and 2 corner fillings, hence 28 per center color and 84 total. Exactly 12 oriented colorings have one reflection symmetry; none has a nonidentity rotational symmetry. Their classes have size 4, while the other 72 colorings have classes of size 8, giving 12 classes.
